notes: 'Stance' here is on the residents' stop-sign request: voting for R23-125 = against the stop sign. Letter A on 2023-06-20 is a merged label; the 0:25:17 turn is mapped to the City Manager per turn.

title: No-parking zone on Chapel Drive for school-bus and pedestrian safety at SRSS
summary: At the Hanover School Division's request, developed with a city employee and RCMP input, council approved no-parking signs on Chapel Drive by the Steinbach Regional Secondary School to improve bus access and visibility of traffic and pedestrians.
status_detail: Approved (R23-204).
figures: About 6-7 parking spaces lost (Zwaagstra, transcript 0:27:50).
notes: Zwaagstra says both '6 to 7 spaces' (0:27:50) and '67 parking spaces' (0:28:19); the latter is likely a transcription of '6, 7'.

title: Council orders a new traffic count at Hespeler St and Loewen Blvd
summary: Councillor Siemens relayed complaints of afternoon backups on Hespeler St at Loewen Blvd (left turns onto Loewen) and asked engineering to look again. The city manager said the 2016-2019 counts had found the intersection within acceptable service levels; council agreed by consensus to a new count at peak times on a school day, with a recommendation.
status_detail: WSP count and engineer's report delivered Apr 16, 2024 (see 2024-hespeler-loewen-three-way-stop).
reasons: engineering-warrant: Earlier counts (2016-2019) found turning movements within tolerance. (Troy Warkentin)
public: Complaints from residents relayed by Siemens and Jake Hiebert, including pedestrians nearly being hit.

title: Truck yard near homes on Tower Ave denied; truck routing discussed
summary: Council unanimously denied a conditional use for a freight/truck yard at 45 Tower Avenue after many neighbours objected (noise, lights, dust, safety, traffic). Staff said trucks would have to use PTH 52, a designated truck route; Councillor Siemens said his first concern was more truck traffic on Main Street.
status_detail: Denied (R24-009). Status refers to the applicant's request.
figures: Applicant had 19 trucks; 4 acres could hold about 60 (minutes Jan 16, 2024 items 22.3, 30).
public: Neighbours (e.g. J.L., S.U., D.M., G.P.) objected; one said it would add a great deal of traffic on Main Street.
notes: Primarily a land-use decision; included for truck-traffic reasoning.

title: Council asks the province for rapid flashing crosswalk lights on Main St and Brandt St
summary: A resident delegation (B.B.) asked for rapid flashing low-level pedestrian lights at two highway crosswalks (Main St near Elmdale School and Brandt St by the bowling alley/7-Eleven), citing a near miss and three years without an answer from MTI. Council unanimously sent a supporting letter. The minister acknowledged the letter (June 2024) and MTI wrote to the resident about a study (Oct 2024).
status_detail: Letter sent (R24-040); provincial replies received as information June 18 and Oct 15, 2024; no installation by end of 2024.
reasons: provincial-highway: Not city jurisdiction; the city can add its voice and publicity. (Michael Zwaagstra); waiting-on-province: 'We'll wait and see what comes of this study.' (Earl Funk)
public: B.B., resident, said MTI promised a study three years earlier and he 'probably never will' hear back; cited Winnipeg and Ste. Anne as having the lights.

title: 2023 traffic count accepted; Superstore/Co-op access flagged next
summary: Council accepted the WSP 2023 count (21 intersections) and forwarded it to MTI. Volumes fell about 1.5% from 2022; PTH 52 at Giesbrecht St and at Lund Road were below the acceptable service level; the study again recommended Giesbrecht signals and improvements at the PTH 12 Superstore/Co-op access as Millbrook Market develops.
status_detail: Accepted and forwarded (R24-054). Superstore/Co-op improvements left for the city to 'continue to monitor'.
figures: Volumes -1.5% year over year (transcript 0:10:58); Park Road West closed during part of the October count (transcript).
reasons: provincial-highway: Highways are provincial; the city's tool is data for lobbying. (Michael Zwaagstra)

title: Residents raise traffic at rezoning hearings; council approves without traffic studies
summary: Residents objecting to infill rezonings cited traffic: Hospital/Home Street (Mar 19, 2024), a fourplex across from SRSS (June 2024) and Giesbrecht Street (Nov 5, 2024). Council approved these; Councillor Bill Hiebert said apartments near his home add little traffic, while Councillor Siemens voted alone against the SRSS fourplex, citing congestion.
status_detail: Rezonings approved (By-law 2241 second reading 4-3 on other grounds; By-law 2217 third reading 6-1, R24-129; By-law 2253 second reading R24-207). No traffic study was asked for.
reasons: development-first: Density belongs beside a school. (Michael Zwaagstra); development-first: Apartments generate little traffic. (Bill Hiebert)
public: Hospital/Home Street residents (e.g. G.W., E.W., D.W.) cited increased traffic and safety at Hospital and Home; G.W. of Giesbrecht Street said the street already has high morning and evening volumes (minutes Nov 5, 2024 item 6.6). Unproven predictions.
notes: 'Stance' here is on approving the developments. By-law 2241's 4-3 split (against: D. Penner, J. Hiebert, Zwaagstra) was not argued on traffic and is not listed as a traffic split vote. Two different 'G.W.' residents are involved (Home St and Giesbrecht St).

title: 3-way stop at Loewen Blvd and Hespeler St defeated 3-4
summary: The WSP count found northbound Hespeler at level of service E, acceptable by the city's standard; the engineer said an all-way stop would help Hespeler at the PM peak but slow Loewen Blvd all day, and advised more data first, suggesting an all-way stop during the Loewen/PTH 12 rebuild detour and a possible future roundabout. Councillor Siemens moved a 3-way stop now; it was defeated 3-4. The mayor said the answer is a roundabout in the long-term capital plan.
status_detail: Motion defeated. No roundabout was budgeted in 2023-2024. Whether a temporary all-way stop was installed during the Loewen/PTH 12 construction was not reported at a council meeting in this period.
figures: Northbound Hespeler LOS E (minutes Apr 16, 2024 item 16.1).
reasons: engineering-warrant: Trust the experts and standards to avoid unintended consequences. (Michael Zwaagstra); study-first: Report recommended more data; 'let the plumbers plumb'. (Damian Penner); engineering-warrant: Rush hour is normal; don't decide on one-off personal experiences; would slow Loewen east-west traffic. (Susan Penner); study-first: A 24-hour change for a 30-45 minute problem; wait for the detour, then build a roundabout. (Earl Funk)
public: Residents' complaints relayed by councillors.
vote: 3-4 (for: Siemens, Jake Hiebert, Bill Hiebert; against: Zwaagstra, Damian Penner, Susan Penner, Funk)

title: Province repairs Main St; no date for PTH 12 resurfacing
summary: The city manager reported MTI's concrete joint repairs on Main Street (Brandt St to Kroeker Ave, 'Craker Avenue' in the transcript) starting May 13, 2024. Councillor Susan Penner asked about rough patches on PTH 12; MTI was considering an asphalt overlay on Brandt St/PTH 12 but had given no timing.
status_detail: No PTH 12 timeline in 2024. (Later: the province began a $24M PTH 12 resurfacing north of Park Road, per the existing report.)
reasons: waiting-on-province: No information on extent or timing. (Troy Warkentin)

title: Elmdale St widened at Reimer Ave for event-centre traffic
summary: Street-widening By-law 2198 for Elmdale Street at Reimer Avenue, tied to the old arena site and the new event centre, passed all three readings so the intersection can be rebuilt for event traffic.
status_detail: Third reading Aug 6, 2024 (R24-161).
mover: Michael Zwaagstra (1st); Bill Hiebert (2nd); Susan Penner (3rd)
notes: The Aug 6 speaker explaining event-centre traffic is unidentified (low confidence) and not quoted.

title: New Traffic By-law 2254: speed limits, school zones, engine-brake ban and higher fines
summary: Council gave first reading to Traffic By-law 2254, which folds the speed-limit and school-zone by-laws into one (adding the new Park Hill school), raises three road sections from 50 to 60 km/h, bans engine retarder brakes with a fine, fines heavy vehicles parked over 2 hours, and doubles parking fines. An administrative penalty by-law to enforce the fines got first reading Dec 17.
status_detail: First reading only in 2024 (R24-213; penalty by-law R24-249). (Adopted January 2025, per the existing report.)
figures: Engine retarder brakes $100 ($50 if paid early); heavy vehicle parked over 2 h $500 ($250); parking tickets from $20/$40 to $40/$80; school zones 30 km/h (package Nov 5, 2024, pp. 43-44 and Schedules A-C).
notes: No transcript of the Nov 5, 2024 meeting exists. The three road sections raised to 60 km/h are highlighted in the draft's Schedule B but could not be identified from the extracted text.

title: Residents' stop-sign request at Harmony Lane and Cutlass Drive: no change; speeding left to the RCMP
themes: stop-sign; calming; speed; enforcement; residents; traffic-study
summary: After a speeding driver killed two dogs being walked on Harmony Lane, residents B.E. and K.E. asked for a stop sign at Cutlass Drive. Councillors Susan Penner and Siemens asked for a review and for other traffic-calming options, but staff said a calming study needed a consultant and had no budget, so council asked only for a stop-sign (warrant) review. The city engineer's review found the existing one-way stop appropriate and council accepted 'no changes', with RCMP asked to patrol for speeders.
status_detail: Consensus Feb 18, 2025 to accept the engineer's report: no new signage. The RCMP staff sergeant agreed (via the RCMP Advisory Committee) to monitor speeds on the street. The wider traffic-calming review was never commissioned.
reasons: no-budget: Evaluating calming measures would need an outside consultant; no budget approved for that. (Troy Warkentin); engineering-warrant: Engineer's count and safety review found the existing stop appropriate; 'no changes are warranted' on every objective criterion. (Troy Warkentin / Michael Zwaagstra); enforcement-not-design: Stop signs are not speed-control devices; speeding is an RCMP enforcement issue. (Troy Warkentin); police-decide: Accepted the report as long as the RCMP monitor and enforce speeds. (Earl Funk)
public: Residents B.E. and K.E. wrote after a speeding car killed their two dogs on Dec 19, 2024, noting many children in the neighbourhood (as related by Councillor S. Penner and the mayor).
notes: Residents' names appear in the transcript and minutes; initials used here.

title: New traffic by-law combines speed limits and school zones, adds Park Hill school zone and higher fines
summary: Council gave second and third reading to Traffic By-law 2254, which merged the speed-limit, reduced-speed school zone and traffic by-laws into one, created a school zone for the new Park Hill elementary school, let city engineering set road classes and spring weight limits, and raised parking and heavy-vehicle fines. Companion By-law 2259 put the new fines into the administrative penalty by-law so they can be enforced.
status_detail: Adopted unanimously Jan 21, 2025 (first reading Nov 2024). By-law 2259 (administrative penalties) adopted the same night.
figures: No dollar figures given in the meeting; fine amounts are in the agenda package (pp. 53-55, per staff, transcript 0:14:28).

title: Loewen Blvd and PTH 12 intersection rebuild finished with the province; city borrows $3M
summary: The cost-shared rebuild of the Loewen Blvd / PTH 12 (Brandt St) intersection was the largest traffic item in the 2025 financial plan, with $3.5M of the city share to be borrowed. The intersection reopened fully in November 2025, and council passed Debt By-law 2270 to borrow $3M over five years at 3.83%, less than budgeted.
status_detail: Intersection 'substantially complete' and open by Dec 16, 2025 (city notice: full operation Nov 24, 2025). By-law 2270 got first and second reading Dec 16, 2025 and third reading Feb 3, 2026 after Municipal Board approval.
figures: 2025 capital program $36.6M incl. Loewen/PTH 12 (finance, Mar 4, 2025, 0:03:33); borrowing budgeted $3.5M (Zwaagstra 0:31:04) at up to 7% (S. Penner Dec 16, 2025, 1:04:08); actual $3M, 5 years, 3.83%, Royal Bank (Warkentin Dec 16, 2025, 1:02:16; Feb 3, 2026, 0:21:14). Mayor called it 'a $14 million intersection' (Mar 4, 2025, 0:29:54); the existing report's final figure is about $11.2M ($5.1M province, $6.1M city).
reasons: provincial-highway: Without the city's share the province would not do the upgrade. (Michael Zwaagstra); traffic-comes-to-steinbach: Growth is what forces highway upgrades. (Michael Zwaagstra)
mover: Michael Zwaagstra (plan; 1st and 3rd reading); Susan Penner (2nd)
seconder: Susan Penner (plan); Jake Hiebert (1st); Bill Hiebert (2nd); Jac Siemens (3rd)
notes: Mayor's '$14 million' (Mar 2025) does not match the ~$11.2M total in the existing report (SteinbachOnline); treat as an estimate.

title: Signals at PTH 52 West and Giesbrecht St: council presses the province until they are working
summary: Traffic signals at PTH 52 West and Giesbrecht Street, first found warranted in 2021 and requested from the province in 2022, kept slipping. In March 2025 staff had no install date; in February 2026 the mayor and Councillor Zwaagstra called for pressure on the province. By September 2026 the province said the lights were going in that year, and SteinbachOnline reported them operating on October 13, 2026.
status_detail: Signals reported operating Oct 13, 2026 (SteinbachOnline; no exact switch-on date given), about 4.5 years after the 2022 request. Councillor Siemens counted them as the city's 14th signalized intersection.
figures: Signalized intersections: 5 in 2006, 13 in 2026 'plus one more coming on this year' (Siemens, Mar 17, 2026, 0:00:10). Cost not published.
reasons: waiting-on-province: MTI's design nearly done but no install date given (Mar 2025). (Troy Warkentin)
public: At a Sept 1, 2026 hearing on 58 Giesbrecht St, residents K.V. and R.V. welcomed the coming lights but worried that left turns into the Tim Hortons would be cut off, pushing traffic onto Giesbrecht and First Street.
notes: Switch-on date is from SteinbachOnline (Oct 2026) as cited in answers/traffic-congestion; not discussed at a recorded meeting before Nov 3, 2026.

title: 2024 traffic count accepted and sent to the province; signal timing on PTH 12 flagged
summary: WSP's 2024 count of the PTH 12 and PTH 52 corridors found flat or falling volumes on most of PTH 12 (affected by construction) and recommended a coordinated signal-timing review with MTI, fixes at the Superstore/Co-op accesses, and monitoring of PTH 52 West at Industrial Road and Lund Road. Council accepted it and forwarded it to Manitoba Transportation and Infrastructure.
status_detail: Accepted and forwarded (R25-060). MTI was said to be reviewing signal timing; the 2025 count (Feb 2026) again recommended retiming three PTH 12 intersections, so the timing fix had not been confirmed.
figures: PTH 12 corridor 1- and 2-year growth both -2.3%; PTH 12 N between PTH 52 W and Main +2.2% over 2023; counts over 4 days late Sept/early Oct 2024 (Warkentin 1:28:23); WSP has done the counts about 27 years.
reasons: provincial-highway: Signal-timing recommendations go to MTI for review; the city cannot retime them. (Troy Warkentin)

title: New Official Community Plan adds active-transportation policy but no transportation master plan
summary: The five-year review of the Official Community Plan (By-law 2244) added policies on active transportation and a first mention of public transportation; the province approved it without amendment. At the April 2025 hearing the mayor said the city would not build designated bike lanes and remains 'the automobile city'; Councillor Siemens called the active-transportation part incomplete. No city-wide transportation or road-network plan was part of the review.
status_detail: Second reading Apr 1, 2025 (R25-070); third reading Sept 16, 2025 (R25-184) after ministerial approval.
reasons: car-first: Bike lanes 'don't work' and slow traffic; vehicles must keep their place on the road. (Earl Funk)
public: Provincial Community Planning welcomed the new active-transportation and public-transportation policies (per WSP consultant at the hearing).
mover: Jac Siemens (R25-069); Jake Hiebert (R25-070); Susan Penner (R25-184)

title: Highway lobbying through the Eastman regional committee: PTH 12 overlay, PTH 12/52/59 upgrades
summary: Councillor Siemens reported that the Eastman Regional Municipal Committee (11-12 municipalities) lobbies the province on highways among other issues: he raised the PTH 12 overlay with the Premier's liaison (Apr 2025) and listed PTH 12, 52 and 59 upgrades and intersections for meetings with regional highway staff (Sept 22, 2025) and Highways Minister Lisa Naylor (Oct 22, 2025). The mayor reported over $500M in added provincial highway funding in the multi-year plan.
status_detail: Lobbying reported; no specific result for Steinbach recorded at council. The province's PTH 12 resurfacing north of Park Road (about $24M, no added lanes) was under way in 2026 per the existing report.
figures: Over $500M in added provincial highway funding (Funk, Apr 15, 2025, 0:00:00).
reasons: provincial-highway: Highways are provincial; regional bloc gets ministers' attention. (Jac Siemens)
notes: Outcome of the Oct 22, 2025 ministerial meeting was not reported at a recorded council meeting.

title: 30 km/h school zone added on Kroeker Ave at Southwood School, beyond staff's advice
summary: Southwood School (Hanover School Division) asked for a reduced-speed school zone on Kroeker Avenue and crossing improvements. Staff scored the site 68/100, within range for either advisory 'school area' signs or a mandatory zone, and recommended signs only. Councillor Zwaagstra amended that to a full school zone, keeping staff's other two recommendations (move the school's fence opening to a safer crossing and cut back sightline-blocking landscaping).
status_detail: Approved unanimously Aug 5, 2025 (R25-154). Staff said a by-law amendment is needed to designate the zone; none was found in the minutes searched through Oct 6, 2026.
figures: Staff score 68 (65-80 qualifies for school area and/or zone) (Zwaagstra 0:17:00).
public: Request letter from Southwood School's principal on behalf of the school, received Apr 15, 2025 and referred to staff.
notes: Jake Hiebert's supporting remarks (0:21:31) are on a low-confidence label; not quoted. Amending by-law not located.

title: First Active Transportation Plan accepted: about $11M of paths, long-term and unfunded
summary: Urban Systems presented the city's first Active Transportation Plan (paths, sidewalks, share-the-road streets and crossings, including a PTH 12 crossing near McKenzie Ave and a path to Superstore). Council accepted it as a guide. Councillor Zwaagstra stressed the roughly $11M total 'won't be happening anytime soon' and that it must not hinder driving.
status_detail: Accepted as a plan in principle (R25-096). No project funding for it was identified in the 2026 financial plan presentation (per existing report); low-cost share-the-road signage was named as a short-term option.
figures: Total about $11M (Zwaagstra 1:03:48); National Active Transportation Fund matches 60% up to $5M (Urban Systems consultant, 0:56:58).
reasons: cost: Price tags 'very high'; most is long-term. (Michael Zwaagstra); car-first: Active transportation must not hinder vehicle traffic; most residents drive. (Michael Zwaagstra)
notes: Separate transit / active-transportation reports exist; included here because members framed it against vehicle traffic.

title: Council backs extra Main Street traffic enforcement with Ste. Anne police, paid by MPI
summary: Reporting from the RCMP Advisory Committee, Councillor Zwaagstra said complaints about racing on Main Street were rising while the detachment was 2-4 officers short, and asked whether council agreed to joint enforcement with the Ste. Anne police, who would also patrol Steinbach on MPI-funded overtime. Council agreed by consensus.
status_detail: Consensus May 6, 2025; Zwaagstra later called it an agreement in force (June 17, 2025). No city cost.
figures: Example cited: 96-97 km/h in a 50 zone on Main Street, $665 fine (Funk 1:17:52).
reasons: police-decide: RCMP shortfall limits enforcement; extra MPI-funded hours fill the gap at no cost to taxpayers. (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: Residents reported racing on Main Street (as relayed by Zwaagstra).

title: Traffic stays an RCMP priority, but the dedicated traffic officer is often pulled away
summary: Council adopted the 2025-26 policing priorities (drugs, property crime, traffic, visibility). Moving them, Councillor Zwaagstra called traffic 'the never-ending one' and recalled the extra traffic officer council funded. In June 2025 he said shortages meant that officer was often called away to other work.
status_detail: Priorities adopted (R25-108). In Sept 2026 the RCMP reported the traffic position back at full duty (see 2026-rcmp-main-street-enforcement).
figures: 18 RCMP members authorized; about 14.5 actually provided (Zwaagstra, June 17, 2025, 0:07:37).
reasons: police-decide: Enforcement depends on RCMP staffing the city cannot control. (Michael Zwaagstra)

title: Siemens repeats his call to end parking on PTH 52, a vote he says he lost
summary: During a hearing on a rental development, Councillor Siemens said he has long wanted all parking removed from PTH 52 (60 km/h) to the fire hall because of rising traffic, but lost that vote on council, and predicted parking will be eliminated eventually.
status_detail: No motion in this period; the earlier vote he refers to was not found in the 2025-2026 minutes.
figures: 60 km/h speed limit on that section (Siemens 0:33:23).
notes: Date of the earlier vote unverified.

title: No traffic study for First Street condos; resident's one-way idea for William Ave turned down
summary: At a hearing on a two-building condo project near First Street, resident R.P. asked whether a traffic impact study had been done, noting William Avenue is barely one lane and that delivery trucks funnel down First Street, and suggested making William one-way. Staff said traffic studies are required only for impacts on PTH 12 and PTH 52, and that First Street is a collector designed for 1,000-4,000 vehicles a day; the mayor backed staff and did not support a one-way.
status_detail: Conditional use approved (R25-248) without a traffic study; one-way not pursued.
figures: Collector street design range 1,000-4,000 vehicles/day (Warkentin 0:37:09).
reasons: provincial-highway: Traffic impact studies are generally required only for impacts on the provincial highways. (Troy Warkentin); engineering-warrant: Engineer saw no traffic concern; existing streets adequate. (Troy Warkentin / Earl Funk)
public: R.P. (First Street resident) asked for a traffic study and a one-way on William Ave for truck traffic; J.G. raised parking and flooding.

title: Resident's request for traffic signs on First Street sent to the RCMP advisory committee
summary: A First Street resident, C.S., wrote asking for signage because of speeds and pedestrian traffic. The mayor suggested policing might be needed and council agreed that the mayor and Councillor Zwaagstra raise it at the RCMP Advisory Committee; the letter was otherwise taken as information.
status_detail: No signage decision; no report back on the RCMP discussion found at later meetings.
reasons: enforcement-not-design: Suggested patrols rather than deciding on signs. (Earl Funk)
public: C.S. (First Street) requested signage for speeding and pedestrian safety.

title: 2025 traffic count: busiest intersection near 3,500 vehicles an hour; retiming advice left to staff and the province
summary: The 2025 WSP count of 20 intersections found PTH 12 at Main Street (PTH 52) carrying nearly 3,500 vehicles at peak hour and a long-term upward trend. It recommended monitoring PTH 52 at Lund Road for possible signals and retiming PTH 12 at Clearspring/Golf, Park Road and Superstore/Co-op. Staff said the recommendations were for 'general consideration' subject to budget; council accepted the report and members said they would press the province.
status_detail: Report accepted (R26-037); council did not adopt the recommendations as direction. Retiming depends on MTI; no result recorded by Nov 2026.
figures: Peak hour at PTH 12 / PTH 52 (Main St) nearly 3,500 vehicles per hour; 20 intersections; counts since 1997 (Warkentin 0:14:17; Zwaagstra 0:21:48).
reasons: provincial-highway: MTI is the authority that manages all signals in Steinbach. (Troy Warkentin); no-budget: Recommendations are subject to further consideration and 'perhaps budget funding'. (Troy Warkentin); traffic-comes-to-steinbach: Counts show traffic comes to Steinbach rather than through it, so a bypass makes no sense to him. (Jac Siemens)
notes: Bypass covered in depth in the separate main-street-bypass report.

title: McKenzie Ave 48-unit rezoning approved over traffic and sidewalk concerns; sidewalk condition not added
summary: Neighbours of a 48-unit rezoning on McKenzie Avenue near PTH 52 raised truck traffic, U-turns at the church, on-street parking blocking the curb lane and no sidewalk on the south side; one suggested a no-stopping zone and moving a mailbox. Councillor Siemens floated a traffic study and asked for a friendly amendment requiring the developer to build a sidewalk to PTH 52; Councillor Damian Penner, the mover, declined. Council approved the rezoning, saying McKenzie is a four-lane through street where most traffic is not local.
status_detail: Second reading Apr 7, 2026 (R26-068) and third reading Sept 1, 2026 (R26-184) without a sidewalk condition or traffic study.
figures: 48 units; 1.5 parking stalls per unit required and provided (Zwaagstra 1:23:24); site about 75 m from the intersection (D. Penner 1:18:37).
reasons: engineering-warrant: Not an engineer; would not add a sidewalk condition that might not be feasible. (Damian Penner); development-first: Density belongs near major intersections and collectors; through traffic, not residents, drives volumes. (Michael Zwaagstra / Damian Penner)
public: H.K., A.R., P.K., J.D. and others (initials) cited congestion, large trucks turning to PTH 52, U-turns near the church, parked cars narrowing a four-lane street, and children with no south-side sidewalk. P.K. proposed a no-stopping zone to PTH 52 and relocating the Canada Post box.
notes: McKenzie Ave is a city street (staff called it an arterial on Oct 6, 2026), not a provincial highway; the mayor's 'highway' refers to its four lanes.

title: Park Hill School parents' traffic-safety request referred to staff; report still pending
summary: The Park Hill School Parent Advisory Council asked council for traffic-safety measures around the new school. Council referred it to administration for a report, expected 'somewhere near summertime'.
status_detail: No report on the request appeared at a recorded meeting through Oct 20, 2026.
reasons: study-first: Staff to review and report before any decision. (Earl Funk)
public: Park Hill School Parent Advisory Council (organization) requested traffic safety measures.

title: Residents ask for traffic studies on infill projects; council relies on street classes and the RCMP
summary: Through 2026, residents at rezoning and variance hearings (Friesen Ave, Stonebridge Crossing, Giesbrecht St, McKenzie Ave, Henry St) asked whether traffic impact studies had been done. None were required for city streets. Council answered with street classifications (collector/arterial capacity), the argument that through traffic dominates, and RCMP enforcement for speeding. Councillor Jake Hiebert was the exception: he asked for a traffic study before a 12-unit building on Henry St near the hospital and voted against it, citing parking and emergency-vehicle access.
status_detail: No traffic study ordered for any of these applications; 288 Henry St rezoning approved 6-1 (R26-200).
figures: McKenzie Ave: four-lane arterial, designed for over 4,000 vehicles a day (Warkentin, Oct 6, 2026, 0:06:00); 58 Giesbrecht: about 12 extra cars (Zwaagstra, Sept 1, 2026, 0:37:35).
reasons: engineering-warrant: Street classification capacity shows the roads can carry the traffic. (Troy Warkentin); development-first: On collectors most traffic is through traffic, not from the new units. (Michael Zwaagstra); enforcement-not-design: Stonebridge problem is speed, handled by the RCMP. (Jac Siemens)
public: P.H. (Friesen Ave, June 2026): trucks and speeders use Friesen as a shortcut from Brandt St. D.J. (Granite Park, July 2026): 'Has a traffic impact assessment been completed?' A.A.: school drop-off parking and traffic on Stonebridge Crossing. K.V./G.W. (Giesbrecht, Sept 2026): Giesbrecht already busy. M.H. and others (McKenzie, Oct 2026): cycling corridor for students, share-the-road signs would be blocked by parking. C.M. (Henry St, Oct 2026): narrow street, parking.
resolution_no: R26-110 (Friesen variance), R26-147 (Bridge Park variance), R26-179 (58 Giesbrecht 2nd), R26-200 (288 Henry 2nd)
vote: R26-200 6-1 (against: Jake Hiebert); R26-147 6-1 (against: Jac Siemens, on height); others unanimous or split on height/parking
notes: Jake Hiebert's Sept 1, 2026 request for a traffic study (1:13:55) is on a medium-confidence label and is paraphrased only. D.J.'s quote is in answers/traffic-congestion (Jul 21, 2026, 0:15:08).

title: Lund Road will not be opened to PTH 52; new units must use Giesbrecht St
summary: At a variance hearing for 80-81 Lund Road, Westview Drive residents asked whether Lund Road would be opened to PTH 52 so new apartments would not funnel traffic past a park. The city manager said the approved concept plan keeps Lund Road closed to the north (to separate industrial and residential uses), with access only via Ellis and Woodhaven Avenues to Giesbrecht Street. Council approved the variance.
status_detail: Variance approved (R26-132); no new connection. The 2025 traffic count separately recommends monitoring PTH 52 at Lund Road for possible signals, which Councillor Siemens opposed in 2025.
reasons: development-first: Access was settled in the earlier rezoning's concept plan. (Troy Warkentin)
public: L.S. and J.W. (Westview Drive) worried about added traffic past a park and asked for Lund Road to be opened to PTH 52; residents at a Sept 1, 2026 hearing (R.V.) had heard it might open to relieve congestion.

title: Williams Creek subdivision gets its own road to Loewen Blvd after Wyndham residents ask for a second exit
summary: Wyndham Estates resident G.W. said the neighbourhood was 'maxed out' on one exit and asked for an immediate second exit before 155 more lots were added. Council approved the Williams Creek subdivision, whose Williams Creek Way connects to Loewen Blvd so construction and new traffic need not pass through Wyndham; Councillor Damian Penner said the congestion would not be significant.
status_detail: Subdivision and road openings approved (R26-157) with Williams Creek Way to Loewen Blvd; no separate second exit for Wyndham itself was ordered.
figures: 153-155 lots (resident and D. Penner).
reasons: engineering-warrant: Traffic 'ebbs and flows'; 155 lots do not create significant congestion. (Damian Penner)
public: G.W. asked for an immediate secondary exit and for construction traffic to avoid Wyndham.
notes: 'Lorne'/'Loam' Boulevard in the transcript is Loewen Boulevard.

title: RCMP: traffic officer back at full duty, targeted Main Street racing blitz
summary: The new RCMP detachment commander (M.M.) reported road safety as a top priority, the municipal traffic services officer back on full duty, fewer traffic complaints, and a targeted Main Street enforcement project using plainclothes GIS officers, with more planned. Councillors Zwaagstra and Siemens asked about catching Main Street racers.
status_detail: Report received; targeted enforcement under way.
figures: 18 municipal positions incl. 1 traffic services investigator; all filled as of Sept 20, 2026 (M.M. 0:05:50).
notes: M.M. is an RCMP official, recorded with role 'staff' for want of a better category.

title: New council: Damian Penner to the RCMP advisory committee, Jake Hiebert to the regional committee
summary: At the Nov 3, 2026 inaugural meeting the mayor named Councillor Damian Penner (with staff member Adam Thiessen) to the RCMP Advisory Committee, replacing the mayor and the retired Councillor Zwaagstra, and Councillor Jake Hiebert to the Eastman Regional Municipal Committee, which lobbies ministers on highways, replacing the retired Councillor Siemens. No traffic items were on the agenda.
status_detail: Appointments made; new councillors Ron Falk and Greg Carlos have no traffic record yet.
notes: Minutes for Nov 3, 2026 not yet available; appointments from transcript.
